clue.text: Use drug at university to increase the tempo

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug
to be up is to be in residence at university, in British usage

explanation.surface: A student is told to take stimulants to get through work faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' is a link word here, inviting you to use the drug as the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed things up is to quicken their pace, as with music played faster.

clue.text: Behaves harshly towards issue coming from another union

definitions.meaning: to step on someone is to treat them harshly
a child of one's spouse by an earlier marriage

explanation.definitionFit: Treading on someone means oppressing them; a husband's or wife's child from an earlier marriage is a stepchild.

clue.text: To embark upon it is recipe for stomach trouble

parts.note: to enter on something is to embark upon it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Starting on something is said to be a sure way to an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe for' links wordplay to definition, as 'a recipe for disaster' leads to a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the intestine causes abdominal pain and diarrhoea.

clue.text: Plan to get medical man back in the navy

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
aft is the sailors' word for the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A scheme to bring a doctor back into naval service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal, but 'back in the navy' is the nautical word for the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary sketch or version of a scheme.

clue.text: Promptly, so the taps can be adjusted

indicators.note: adjusting the letters means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A plumber says the taps can be fixed quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old word for with all speed, immediately.

clue.text: Wash follows sailor on Saturday — and Sunday perhaps?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it
follows says this piece comes after the ones before it

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for Saturday
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a bath is a wash

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a bath on Saturday, and perhaps Sunday too.
explanation.walkthrough: The holy day of rest is Saturday for Jews and Sunday for most Christians, so the question mark marks Sunday as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian day of rest and worship is commonly called the Sabbath.

clue.text: Cut sound — that's fine

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as wool from sheep

explanation.surface: A remark that a haircut's noise is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' links wordplay to definition. Sheer fabric is fine and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer stockings or curtains are of very fine, thin, see-through material.

clue.text: Flat on one's back and bottom, having been on horse

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea
ridden is the past participle of ride, as on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider ends up lying flat out with a sore backside after time in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'Flat'. 'bottom' suggests the backside, but it is a river bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bedridden is confined to bed, lying down through illness.

clue.text: A long time to set up theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Building a playhouse takes a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to set up' turns AN ERA, read upwards, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest or display, as a theatre of war is a field of action.

clue.text: Others differ about liberal case for keeping weaponry

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the liberal letter
differ says these letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Others disagree with a liberal over the case for having guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differ' rearranges OTHERS into HOSTER, and 'about' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather sheath for carrying a pistol.

clue.text: Unusually spare

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, ... means exceptionally, as in ... large
a spare item is one more than needed, a surplus one

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an intensifying adverb meaning exceptionally, and as an adjective for something additional or surplus.

clue.text: Spell weed variety thus: Veronica

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener names a kind of weed, spelling it out for us: Veronica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' is a link word. Veronica is the botanical genus of the plant, with small blue flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the Latin genus name of the small blue-flowered garden plant.

clue.text: One who spreads litter

definitions.meaning: someone or something that stretches things out wider
a litter is a frame for carrying a sick or wounded person

explanation.definitionFit: A person who stretches things spreads them; a litter for carrying the wounded is the same word for a portable bed.

clue.text: Not suitable in a training exercise

parts.note: taken as written
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are unfit to join a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unfitting or inappropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: Famous comment by old copper

parts.note: a note is a brief remark or comment
d was the symbol for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A celebrated remark was made by a retired policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the coin: d stood for a penny in Britain's pre-1971 money.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted person is well known or celebrated.

clue.text: Device for dropping beams falls on sorceress

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: dips means drops or falls
a witch is a woman who practises sorcery

explanation.surface: A gadget to drop rafters lands on a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's dipswitch lowers the headlamp beams to stop dazzling oncoming drivers.

clue.text: Admirer conceals plot from journalist

indicators.note: conceals means the admirer word holds the plot word hidden inside it

parts.note: a suitor is a man who courts and admires a woman
a bed is a garden plot for plants

explanation.surface: A lovestruck admirer hides a scheme from a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a scheme, but it is a garden plot, a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor is a newspaper journalist who checks and corrects copy.

clue.text: Tapster reveals skill during drinkingbout

indicators.note: during means the skill sits inside the drinking bout

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree, printed here as 'drinking bout'
art is a skill or craft

explanation.surface: A barman shows his skill during a boozing session.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws and serves beer in a pub.

clue.text: Delay rate Increase

parts.note: tempo is the rate or speed of music
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Putting off a rise in the interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or play for time by avoiding a decision.

clue.text: New paper, said to leave no trace

indicators.note: new tells us to make these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new newspaper is reported to have vanished without trace.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to leave no sign behind.

clue.text: Provided clothing came into line

definitions.meaning: soldiers dressing ranks line up straight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means clothed, and in drill, troops dress to align themselves in a straight row.

clue.text: Larva has necessary wings and speed

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: An insect grub is given the wings and speed it needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The immature stage of insects such as dragonflies is called a nymph, a larval form.

clue.text: A place of concealment under the skin. Stumped?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece under another is placed below it

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
stumped is a way a cricket batsman is out

explanation.surface: Something hidden beneath the skin baffles the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' looks like 'puzzled', but in cricket a batsman stumped by the wicketkeeper is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a secret refuge where someone lies low.

clue.text: English umpires' decision when there's nothing in it is joint

indicators.note: in it means the nothing is placed inside the umpires' decision

parts.note: LBW, leg before wicket, is a cricket umpire's ruling of out
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A cricket match where the umpires' verdict is a close call.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, LBW (leg before wicket) is a way of being given out by the umpire.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinged joint between upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Express disapproval over way increase comes out

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: People jeer at the way a price rise is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is a lift or rise in amount.

clue.text: Wears out the War Office, taking road to damnation perhaps?

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of order

parts.note: WO is the abbreviation for War Office

explanation.surface: Someone wears down the War Office officials, taking the road to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WEARS into SWEAR. 'Damnation!' is an example of a curse, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation used as an exclamation is an example of a mild curse or oath.

clue.text: Pulls up grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: draws means pulls, as a cart

explanation.surface: Someone tugs up turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, turf.

clue.text: Controls section of legislature in Switzerland

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Power rests with part of the Swiss parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps by which a rider guides a horse, so they stand for control.

clue.text: Secretarial skill is little help

parts.note: short means little in length
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A remark that a secretary's ability is of small assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in quick symbols for dictation was a standard office skill of typists.

clue.text: Jones (from building) is blue but not dead

indicators.note: not means the dead letter is removed from the colour

parts.note: indigo is a deep blue colour

explanation.surface: A man named Jones, from the building trade, is sad but alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect, so 'from building' points to his profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect Inigo Jones designed the Banqueting House in Whitehall.

clue.text: Many in Rome longed to be abandoned

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Many people in the Italian capital yearned to be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'Rome'. 'to be' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to discard or leave it behind.

clue.text: Appreciation for detail

definitions.meaning: a particular point, as in 'in every way and in this one'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means esteem or high regard, and also a particular point, as in 'correct in every particular'.
